articles.title: Josh Allen makes major promise to Buffalo Bills teammates after surviving ugly win over Patrick Mahomes and Chiefs
articles.summary: Josh Allen did not try to hide his frustration after the Buffalo Bills escaped with a 13-10 Thanksgiving win over the Kansas City Chiefs.
articles.body: Josh Allen did not try to hide his frustration after the Buffalo Bills escaped with a 13-10 Thanksgiving win over the Kansas City Chiefs. The quarterback threw two interceptions and managed just 81 passing yards in difficult conditions at Highmark Stadium. While Tyler Bass delivered a decisive 57-yard field goal in the closing seconds, Allen knew his performance had put unnecessary pressure on his teammates. After the game, he made a direct promise to the locker room, accepting responsibility for his recent struggles and insisting that better performances were coming.Josh Allen accepts responsibility after difficult Chiefs winJosh Allen's numbers against Kansas City told a story he could not ignore. The Bills quarterback completed only 10 of 21 passes for 81 yards, threw two interceptions and took two sacks for a net loss of 17 yards. He failed to throw a touchdown and finished with an 18.3 passer rating.It was another frustrating outing for the reigning MVP, who had also thrown two interceptions against the Miami Dolphins in Buffalo's previous game. Two consecutive performances with multiple turnovers raised concerns about his decision-making, particularly with the playoffs approaching.Allen did not attempt to shift the blame when reporters asked about his display. Instead, he acknowledged that he had not played well over the past two games and made it clear that the responsibility rested with him.“I have to be better. I will be better,” Allen said, via reporter Matthew Bove.The quarterback also addressed the conditions at Highmark Stadium. Rain and strong winds made passing difficult throughout the night, creating one of the toughest weather situations he had experienced during his career.However, Allen refused to use the conditions to defend his performance.“Allen went on to say he hasn’t played well for two games. Said it was one of the worst weather games he’s played in but it’s not an excuse because everyone had to play in it,” Bove noted.That response offered a glimpse into Allen's mindset. He understood that the Bills could not afford another performance filled with careless mistakes, especially against stronger opponents later in the season.Buffalo's supporting cast gives Allen a chance to respondAllen's struggles made the contributions of his teammates even more important. Running back James Cook carried much of the offensive responsibility, finishing with 117 rushing yards on 32 attempts and scoring Buffalo's only touchdown on the ground.Allen also contributed 43 rushing yards on seven carries, while Khalil Shakir led the Bills' limited passing attack with three catches for 33 yards.Buffalo's defense also deserves credit. Patrick Mahomes completed 16 of 29 passes for 174 yards without a touchdown. The Chiefs struggled to find consistent offensive rhythm, allowing Buffalo to remain in contention despite Allen's mistakes.Bass eventually took care of the rest. His 54-yard field goal tied the game before his 57-yard kick secured the victory in the final seconds.The result extended Buffalo's winning streak to seven games and improved its record to 10-1, keeping the Bills at the top of the AFC standings.For Allen, however, the bigger task begins with the next game. Buffalo has enough quality around him to survive an occasional off night, but its championship ambitions will depend heavily on its quarterback delivering more consistent performances. His promise was clear. Now his teammates need to see it reflected on the field.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers goes unclaimed by all 31 NFL teams after explosive Pittsburgh Steelers exit; 42-year-old quarterback becomes a free agent following public fallout with Mike McCarthy
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II criticized Aaron Rodgers in an interview with Gerry Dulac.
articles.body: Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II criticized Aaron Rodgers in an interview with Gerry Dulac. “He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don’t do that to your teammates a couple of days before the game, that’s for sure.” What did Rodgers do?He went public with explosive attacks against head coach Mike McCarthy just days before the Steelers game against the Denver Broncos.The 42-year-old quarterback allegedly accused McCarthy of sleeping and snoring during multiple meetings, missing practices, walkthroughs, and film study, and mistakenly saying, “One, two, three, Packers!” instead of “One, two, three, Steelers!” at Steelers vs. Philadelphia Eagles halftime. Rodgers wanted to take over offensive playcalling, but McCarthy denied that. Rooney also told Dulac that Mike McCarthy is “as healthy as the rest of us” and added: “I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond.”Aaron Rodgers went from being benched to waived in 48 hoursOn Nov. 23, a reporter asked Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy if he’d give other quarterbacks, like Mason Rudolph, a chance to play after two consecutive losses with Rodgers as the starter. McCarthy wholeheartedly chose Rodgers above all.The next day, on Nov. 24, McCarthy benched Rodgers and started Mason Rudolph for Friday night vs. the Denver Broncos. The next day, on Nov. 25, Rodgers missed the morning team meeting; owner Art Rooney II said that the franchise wasn’t going to beg Rodgers to stay.“If he believes his future lies elsewhere, he is free to leave. I promise you, we are not going to miss him,” Rooney told reporters.“We have other quality players in this squad, and we believe in the team we’re building. No individual is bigger than the franchise.Aaron is welcome to stay, but he must understand that decisions made by the coaching staff and management deserve respect. If he wants to remain a part of this project, he must be willing to follow the manager’s vision.”Pat McAfee interviewed Rodgers on The Pat McAfee Show the same day he missed the team meeting [Nov. 25], where the Mike McCarthy allegations surfaced. The same day, on Nov. 25, the Steelers waived Rodgers. He cleared waivers and became a free agent on Nov. 26.Wednesday morning - missed team meeting.Wednesday afternoon - Pat McAfee interview.Wednesday night - waived by the team.Why have teams not claimed Aaron Rodgers?It has been over a day since the veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers has gone unclaimed by all 31 teams. If we look at why each team has chosen not to sign him, several reasons might come up.For instance, some teams might think he’s like Brandon Aiyuk of the San Francisco 49ers, who disrespects the franchise and the coaching staff. Some teams might not want to risk a veteran quarterback at such a crucial midseason time. Some teams are happy just the way they are - they already have a starting quarterback.Dianna Russini, a former The Athletic reporter, asked several teams but there was no taker at the moment. Injuries can change situations in a second, but if this is Rodgers’ final season, his options seem limited.According to Steelers Depot’s Alex Kozora, the New England Patriots could theoretically have interest. Drake Maye is out. Tommy DeVito is the starter. But there’s no indication that the team’s interested.The Baltimore Ravens traded for Arizona Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett, and the Minnesota Vikings traded for Las Vegas Raiders QB Kirk Cousins, so they may not want to add another veteran either.San Francisco 49ers and Green Bay Packers linked to Aaron RodgersCBS Sports’ Bryan DeArdo predicts the San Francisco 49ers and the Green Bay Packers as the two possible destinations for the four-time NFL MVP. The 49ers could be nostalgic for Aaron Rodgers as he’s a California native and grew up a San Francisco 49ers fan.The 49ers passed on him in the 2005 NFL Draft, when the Green Bay Packers selected him as the first round 24th overall pick. If he enters the Bay, he may have to serve as a backup for Brock Purdy. Kyle Shanahan might want him considering his extensive experience.As for the Packers, that would be a homecoming for Rodgers. Of course, without Mike McCarthy - his fellow Super Bowl winning head coach.As per CBS Sports’ Bryan DeArdo, Rodgers is on good terms with both current Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur and quarterback Jordan Love. Plus, the timing couldn’t have been more perfect.This is seemingly his last season in the league, and what better way to close his NFL chapter than by retiring as a Green Bay Packer - just like he entered the league in the first place. If things don’t pan out and he remains unsigned midseason, he could very well retire.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: "Nobody wins when the family feuds": Tom Brady calls out Aaron Rodgers for breaking an unwritten NFL locker room rule amid Mike McCarthy controversy
articles.summary: Tom Brady has made his position clear on Aaron Rodgers' bitter Pittsburgh Steelers exit, questioning the quarterback's decision to take his disagreements
articles.body: Tom Brady has made his position clear on Aaron Rodgers' bitter Pittsburgh Steelers exit, questioning the quarterback's decision to take his disagreements with Mike McCarthy into the public domain. Speaking during Fox Sports' coverage of the Philadelphia Eagles-Dallas Cowboys Thanksgiving game, Brady stressed that an NFL locker room should remain a place of trust, even when players and coaches disagree. While he acknowledged Rodgers' Hall of Fame career, the former New England Patriots quarterback suggested that personal grievances should never outweigh responsibility towards teammates and the organisation.Tom Brady questions Aaron Rodgers' decision to make Steelers dispute publicAaron Rodgers' departure from Pittsburgh quickly turned into a public dispute after the Steelers announced late Tuesday that they would bench him and start Mason Rudolph against the Denver Broncos. The decision came as a surprise, but Rodgers' response made the situation considerably more complicated.During an appearance on Pat McAfee's show, Rodgers launched a series of criticisms against McCarthy, questioning his preparation, leadership and understanding of the game. He alleged that the coach had fallen asleep during meetings, failed to watch enough film and even mistakenly led a "1-2-3, Packers!" chant at halftime.Reports also suggested Rodgers wanted play-calling responsibilities and gave Pittsburgh an ultimatum: grant his demand or release him. McCarthy subsequently confirmed that Rodgers "made an ultimatum." The Steelers chose to move on, officially releasing the veteran quarterback soon after his interview.Brady did not question Rodgers' ability or achievements. His criticism was directed at how the situation unfolded and what it said about the responsibilities players carry inside a team."The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it's a very sacred place. We shouldn't ever lose track of that as players. It's a privilege to be in that locker room. You're fighting with your teammates, you're fighting with your coaches, you're always acting as a team together. Shouldn't always be the place for private things to become public, that's what I'll say."Brady also made a distinction between individual success and being a dependable teammate. He believes the latter should take priority, regardless of a player's standing in the league."Certainly a Hall of Fame career and he's a tremendous player and it has nothing to do with his play-style. I was fortunate to be around a lot of great teammates over the years, and what made a great teammate to me was you cared about your teammates and your coaches, and you cared about what your team was trying to accomplish. That supersedes any individual aspect of your game that you want to promote."He finished his point with a line that captured his frustration with the entire episode: "Nobody wins when the family feuds."Rob Gronkowski highlights how Tom Brady handled coaching disagreementsTom Brady's comments carry additional weight because he also experienced difficult relationships with coaches during his career. His partnership with Bill Belichick in New England was not without friction. The quarterback acknowledged last year that a "natural tension" developed between them, which only ended when he left the Patriots.However, their disagreements rarely spilled into public arguments. Brady continued to acknowledge Belichick's contribution to their success, even after their professional relationship ended.He also reflected on that period while discussing the Rodgers situation, admitting neither man was perfect but emphasising the relationships they built along the way."I wasn't a perfect player and he wasn't a perfect coach, but we did some things in the game that we're so proud of now," Brady said. He added that his relationships with teammates and coaches meant more to him than winning Super Bowl trophies.Rob Gronkowski, Brady's former Patriots teammate, offered a similar assessment earlier on Thursday. He questioned whether Rodgers would get another NFL opportunity, suggesting that teams might be reluctant to bring in the controversy surrounding the veteran quarterback.Gronkowski also recalled how Brady dealt with disagreements behind closed doors."I've seen situations personally with my own eyes where [Brady] and coaches had disagreements. But there's one thing that Tom did different. He would dissect it all and then he would hold it in. And he would still do what's best for the team and for his teammates and for the organization."Tom Brady played under three head coaches during his NFL career: Belichick in New England, followed by Bruce Arians and Todd Bowles in Tampa Bay. His relationship with Belichick was particularly significant, making his comments more than a general lecture about team culture.Rodgers and McCarthy also have considerable history. Their partnership began in Green Bay in 2006 and eventually produced a Super Bowl title. McCarthy's appointment in Pittsburgh created the possibility of another chapter between the two, but their reunion ended in a public fallout instead.For Brady, the bigger disappointment appears to be how a professional disagreement became a public spectacle. His message was not that players should never challenge coaches. It was that those disagreements should not come at the expense of the people sharing the locker room.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: "End of a legendary career": Aaron Rodgers' NFL legacy takes a troubling hit after explosive Steelers exit and accusations of quitting on his team
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers' turbulent exit from Pittsburgh has left the NFL with more questions than answers.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers' turbulent exit from Pittsburgh has left the NFL with more questions than answers. Now, former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin has offered an emotional assessment of the situation, raising the possibility that football fans may have witnessed the final chapter of one of the sport's most remarkable careers. The four-time MVP's public dispute with Mike McCarthy has clearly struck a nerve with Tomlin, who knows both men. His reaction also reflects how much Rodgers' departure could mean for the Steelers and the league.Mike Tomlin reacts to Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy's public falloutSpeaking to Mike Tirico during NBC Sports' coverage of Thursday night's Chiefs-Bills game, Tomlin admitted that watching the dispute unfold brought mixed emotions. However, sadness stood out above everything else.“I had a range of emotions watching the course of events yesterday,” Tomlin told Mike Tirico at halftime of Thursday night's Chiefs-Bills game.He then shared a more sobering thought about Rodgers' future, suggesting that the quarterback's career could be approaching its conclusion.“I think the prevailing one is just general sadness. Sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career in the quarterback, Aaron Rodgers. And just on a macro level, whether it's organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum, those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football.”Tomlin's comments carry particular weight because he spent 19 seasons leading Pittsburgh and worked with Rodgers during the quarterback's time with the franchise.The situation escalated after Rodgers publicly criticised McCarthy, bringing up concerns about missed meetings, a quarterback discussion and an unusual moment during a halftime huddle. McCarthy disputed parts of Rodgers' account, while Steelers president Art Rooney II publicly backed the head coach.Tomlin also expressed frustration with how the dispute became public.“I'm upset about it. It's a dumpster fire, and I don't say that in a judgmental way. I presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years.”Aaron Rodgers faces an uncertain future after Steelers departureRodgers' departure has raised fresh questions about whether he will get another opportunity in the NFL. The 42-year-old was benched in favour of Mason Rudolph before Pittsburgh released him. He subsequently cleared waivers, leaving him free to sign with another team.His numbers this season show that he can still contribute. Rodgers recorded 2,241 passing yards and 16 touchdowns across 10 games. Last season, he threw for 3,322 yards and 24 touchdowns as Pittsburgh won the AFC North before losing to Houston in the wild-card round.However, his on-field production is now competing with the controversy surrounding his departure.Former NFL star Michael Irvin was particularly critical of Rodgers, questioning his commitment to Pittsburgh.“Did he quit on this team? My answer's a yes. Absolutely,” Irvin said.He added: “We work together. We put in sweat together. We bleed together. We hurt together. To me, that's quitting on your team.”Irvin also described the ending as “a stain” on Rodgers' career.Rodgers has previously indicated that this would be his final NFL season. While another team could still offer him an opportunity, Tomlin's comments underline the possibility that his remarkable career may be approaching its end.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Buffalo Bills' new $2.1 billion stadium faces backlash as viral videos appear to show water leaks and flooding during Thanksgiving showdown against Patrick Mahomes' Kansas City Chiefs
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills had plenty to celebrate after edging out Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving.
articles.body: The Buffalo Bills had plenty to celebrate after edging out Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving. But away from the result, their new $2.1 billion home became the centre of an unexpected controversy. Videos shared online appeared to show water collecting inside parts of Highmark Stadium, with some footage raising questions about possible leaks and drainage. For a venue built to deliver a modern NFL experience, the scenes were difficult to ignore. Fans quickly turned their attention from the game to the stadium itself.Highmark Stadium faces questions after viral flooding videosThe Thanksgiving matchup brought challenging weather to Buffalo, with heavy rain and strong winds affecting conditions throughout the evening. While the players battled on the field, footage from inside the stadium began circulating on social media. Some clips appeared to show water gathering in public areas, while others prompted concerns about dripping water and how well the venue handled the downpour.The timing made the criticism even sharper. The new Highmark Stadium opened in August 2026 after a reported investment of around $2.1 billion. Expectations were naturally high for a project of that scale. Fans expect more than impressive architecture from a new NFL venue. They also want a comfortable and reliable place to watch games, particularly when the weather turns unpleasant.The stadium features a partial canopy, but its open-air design leaves the playing field exposed. That decision has now returned to the spotlight, with supporters questioning whether the venue should have included a retractable roof.Bills stadium's open-air design sparks criticism during Chiefs gameThe debate is not limited to the videos showing apparent water problems. The stadium's ability to handle severe weather has also become a talking point. Local weather coverage described persistent rain and strong winds around the venue, creating difficult conditions for spectators and players.There is also a wider question about the money involved. A retractable roof would have added to the construction cost, but the current situation has led some fans to revisit whether that investment would have been worthwhile.On the field, Buffalo managed to overcome the conditions and secure a 13-10 victory over Kansas City. The result gave Bills supporters a Thanksgiving win, but the stadium controversy quickly became another talking point.For a venue that represents such a major investment, the viral footage has created an uncomfortable first impression during a high-profile weather test. However, the clips alone do not establish a structural defect, and the reported leaks still need proper verification. The Bills and stadium authorities may now face growing pressure to explain what happened and whether any improvements are needed.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce's $200 million Garage Beer turned one million cheese balls into an unusual charity marketing spectacle
articles.summary: Jason and Travis Kelce have found an unusual way to bring their business and charitable interests together.
articles.body: Jason and Travis Kelce have found an unusual way to bring their business and charitable interests together. Their Garage Beer brand joined forces with snack company Utz for a Million Cheese Ball Challenge, turning a giant pool of snacks into an attraction at a major Eagles Autism Foundation fundraiser. The idea was simple but certainly not ordinary. Participants had to search through more than one million cheese balls for hidden, branded ping-pong balls. Behind the playful stunt was a bigger effort to support a cause close to Jason Kelce and his family.Garage Beer and Jason Kelce bring an unusual twist to charity fundraisingThe Million Cheese Ball Challenge became one of the eye-catching attractions at the 2026 Beer Bowl, an annual fundraising event hosted by Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie, in support of the Eagles Autism Foundation.The activation brought together Garage Beer and Utz, with participants searching through a massive collection of cheese balls for orange ping-pong balls carrying Garage Beer branding. The challenge gave guests an entertaining way to take part in the event while helping draw attention to its charitable purpose.For Garage Beer, the partnership also offered a different way to connect with customers. Rather than relying only on conventional advertising, the brand became part of an experience that combined food, entertainment and fundraising.Jason and Travis Kelce co-own Garage Beer, making the event another example of how the brothers are building their business identity beyond their NFL careers. Their involvement gives the brand a recognisable sporting connection, while Jason's participation in the Beer Bowl brings a personal element to its charity work.Jason and Travis Kelce's Garage Beer connection meets a $1.26 million charity effortThe challenge was part of a much larger fundraising effort. Jason and Kylie Kelce's Team 62 activities raised $1.26 million for the Eagles Autism Foundation in 2026. The organisation has now raised more than $3.69 million through its fundraising efforts since 2021.The Beer Bowl was one of several activities supporting the cause. The wider programme also included community events, an All Abilities clinic and an online auction.The Eagles Autism Foundation supports programmes focused on autism research, care and community inclusion. Its work gives the annual fundraiser a purpose that extends well beyond a single event.Garage Beer's involvement also highlights how Jason and Travis are using their growing business platform to reach audiences outside football. The brothers have turned their popularity into a shared business venture, but partnerships like this show another side of that expansion.The Million Cheese Ball Challenge may have looked like a light-hearted attraction, but it helped put a serious charitable mission in front of a much wider audience.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “Gratitude is contagious”: Gisele Bundchen celebrates Thanksgiving with Tom Brady’s kids and her son with Joaquim Valente
articles.summary: Apart from her usual sunset-y, rainbow-y, beachy, and birdy pictures, Gisele Bundchen offered a rare glimpse into her three kids with two men - Tom Brady
articles.body: Apart from her usual sunset-y, rainbow-y, beachy, and birdy pictures, Gisele Bundchen offered a rare glimpse into her three kids with two men - Tom Brady and Joaquim Valente.The three children have developed a rare sibling bond that defies normal step-sibling expectations. The blended family’s boundless love can easily be depicted in the 14 snapshots that Tom Brady’s ex-wife shared on her Instagram to commemorate Thanksgiving Day. The 46-year-old Brazilian supermodel captioned the post:“The amount of goodness we experience in life depends on our ability to notice it. Gratitude is contagious, and the more we can appreciate the beauty around us, the more joy we bring into our lives and the lives of others.May we always find something to be grateful for, not just today, but every day. Happy Thanksgiving! Sending you all so much love.”Gisele Bundchen gives rare glimpse into blended family with Tom Brady’s kids and Joaquim ValenteEven a five-year age gap between siblings is enough to make the older sibling feel parental toward the younger one.Now consider a 12 or 15-plus-year gap between step-siblings. They wouldn’t just feel parental - they would also get practical parenting tips, because they are closer to the age of becoming parents themselves and much farther from the age of being toddlers or young kids themselves. Just speculation.Anyhow, Gisele Bundchen’s kids with NFL legend Tom Brady - Benjamin Rein Brady, 16, and Vivian Lake Brady, 13 - posed with Bundchen’s one-year-old son with Joaquim Valente - whose name starts with the letter “A” and whose middle name is “River.”One image showed the trio sitting together while Gisele’s young son clung to his big sister, Vivian, in a warm embrace. Vivian looked at Benjamin while Benjamin tried to explain something to Gisele’s young son with a show of hands.In another picture, Vivian cuddled up to her baby brother and placed a kiss on his tiny head as they traveled on an airplane. In a third picture, Benjamin carried his little brother into his arms while looking at LED lights on the wall, with Gisele’s young son merrily enjoying the colorful light show.The health guru posed with her 21-month-old son on the beach during a family vacation - one picture taken during the day and the other during the evening sunset.Gisele Bundchen didn’t cover her young son with Joaquim Valente’s face with a heartOne of the humble photos offered a glimpse of River feeding a carrot to a cute little rabbit. He could have stopped by while cycling - courtesy of his helmet.And, as always, it was the last picture that had the family of three -Gisele with her second husband and Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu instructor, Joaquim Valente, and their almost two-year-old son, whose name starts with “A” and has “River” as his middle name - by the watery beach, on the white sand, with coconut trees on one side and crystal-clear blue water on the other side.The most surprising part of this Thanksgiving special slide in Gisele’s photo collection? She did not hide/cover any of her young son’s pictures with hearts, even if some of them showed glimpses of his side profile. Maybe she’s finally okay with posting her baby boy’s pictures online. Unlike some.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Brittany Mahomes’ ‘What a Joke’ Rant Takes Aim at NFL Referees After Controversial Chiefs Bills Call
articles.summary: Brittany Mahomes was furious with the referees after the Kansas City Chiefs suffered a painful 13-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Thursday night.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes was furious with the referees after the Kansas City Chiefs suffered a painful 13-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Thursday night. A disputed catch call against Rashee Rice stopped a late Chiefs drive, leaving Patrick Mahomes and his teammates with little time to respond. Following the game, Brittany took to Instagram to express her frustration, questioning the officials’ decision and openly criticizing the call that hurt Kansas City.Brittany Mahomes calls out NFL referees after Rashee Rice’s controversial catchThe controversy unfolded during Kansas City’s late offensive drive when Patrick Mahomes connected with Rashee Rice on a third-and-10 play from the Chiefs’ own 9-yard line. Rice appeared to make an 11-yard catch beyond the first-down marker, which could have helped Kansas City keep its hopes alive in the closing minutes.However, the officials reviewed the play and overturned the initial ruling, deciding that Rice had not maintained possession of the football as he went to the ground. The decision turned the play into an incomplete pass, forcing the Chiefs to stop their drive and eventually punt.Brittany Mahomes did not hide her anger after watching the decision. She shared a strongly worded message on her Instagram story late Thursday night, writing, “HAHAHAHAHAHA WHAT A JOKE,” before adding, “Guess we can’t even play football without getting it called against us… not sure what an actual catch is after that I guess? I don’t wanna hear s**t anymore from anyone.”She also shared posts from other people who questioned the ruling and supported Rice’s catch. One of the posts criticized an unusual scene involving an official standing near a heater on the Bills’ sideline while Buffalo players were around him.The decision drew attention from the Chiefs’ players and coaching staff as well, with Patrick Mahomes and Rice both believing the receiver had completed the catch.Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes question referees’ decision in Chiefs-Bills lossRice was asked whether he thought he had caught the ball, and he answered, “Yes, I did.” Patrick Mahomes also reportedly believed Rice had completed the play and said he thought the officials were reviewing the spot rather than questioning whether the receiver had possession.The NFL offered its explanation after the review. Mark Butterworth, the league’s vice president of instant replay, said the officials believed Rice lost control of the ball as he went to the ground.“As the receiver was going to the ground, he had the ball in his right hand and when he contacted the ground, his hand slid up the ball and we deemed that a loss of control,” Butterworth said, according to ESPN. “The hand moving up the ball is what we deemed the loss of control.”Chiefs head coach Andy Reid was also unhappy with the ruling and questioned what the officials had seen during the review.“I’m not quite sure what they saw,” Reid said, according to ESPN. “I saw he had control of the ball and his elbow hit and then the ball hit the turf but he had control. Normally in those situations, it’s got to be clear and obvious. To me, that was not clear and obvious.”The overturned call stopped Kansas City’s possession, although it remains unclear whether the Chiefs would have scored had the catch stood. Buffalo later failed to capitalize on its next possession, while Kansas City also struggled to move the ball.After another Chiefs punt, a 17-yard return gave Buffalo an opportunity to attempt a long field goal. Tyler Bass then made a 57-yard kick as time expired, handing the Bills a 13-10 win and adding another painful moment to Kansas City’s night.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Former Vikings punter Chris Kluwe called MAGA a "Nazi movement" may flip deep-red California seat blue
articles.summary: Former Minnesota Vikings punter Chris Kluwe declares victory in California's 72nd Assembly District, reportedly ending a 36-year Republican hold.
articles.body: There were many shocking flips in the midterms, but one of the most improbable could be former Minnesota Vikings punter and LGBTQ+ activist Chris Kluwe, who was arrested at a Huntington Beach City Council meeting in 2025 after comparing the MAGA movement to Nazism, segregation, and homophobia, heading to California’s state legislature. The outspoken anti-Trump activist declared victory in California’s 72nd Assembly District, reportedly ending a 36-year Republican hold on the seat. I say reportedly because as of Tuesday night, Kluwe led with 110,539 votes (50.21%) of the total. Van Der Mark was more than 900 votes behind with 109,615 votes (49.79%) As of Thanksgiving Day, approximately 1,300 ballots reportedly remained to be counted. The results of the election must be certified by December 3rd. The fact that it's taken this long to count a reported less than 250,000 votes is certifiably insane, in my opinion, but I digress. CALIFORNIA’S SLUGGISH VOTE COUNTING RIPPED ACROSS THE POLITICAL SPECTRUM: 'EXTREMELY EMBARRASSING' "I promise to represent everyone, while never losing sight of who I work for and why I decided to run in the first place," Kluwe said in a public statement declaring his victory on Wednesday. We should take that promise to represent everyone with a massive grain of salt given his previous rhetoric about Trump and the MAGA movement. In February 2025, Kluwe made national headlines after delivering a tirade during a Huntington Beach City Council meeting over a proposed plaque commemorating the 50th anniversary of the city’s public library. The plaque featured an acrostic spelling MAGA, with the letters standing for "Magical, Alluring, Galvanizing, Adventurous." Kluwe used his allotted public comment time to condemn the Trump administration and its political movement, describing MAGA as "profoundly corrupt" and a "Nazi movement." He also compared Trump's signature campaign apparel to Nazi symbolism, saying that Trump "replaced a swastika with a red hat." He did not stop there. "MAGA stands for trying to erase trans people from existence. MAGA stands for resegregation and racism. MAGA stands for censorship and book bans. MAGA stands for firing air traffic controllers while planes are crashing," Kluwe said. "MAGA stands for firing the people overseeing our nuclear arsenal. MAGA stands for firing military veterans and those serving them at the VA, including canceling research on veteran suicide. MAGA stands for cutting funds to education, including for disabled children. "MAGA is profoundly corrupt, unmistakably antidemocracy, and most importantly, MAGA is explicitly a Nazi movement. You may have replaced a swastika with a red hat, but that is what it is." After delivering his remarks, Kluwe announced that he would engage in "peaceful civil disobedience" before approaching the council dais. He was subsequently arrested and carried out of the chambers by police officers. The incident reportedly cost the former NFL punter his football coaching job at Edison High School, where he had worked since 2019. GOP WIPEOUT GOES FROM BAD TO WORSE AS DEMS QUIETLY SCORE ANOTHER MAJOR WIN WITH BIG RAMIFICATIONS Now, less than two years after his arrest, Kluwe is poised to represent a historically Republican district that encompasses Huntington Beach, Newport Beach, Seal Beach, Laguna Beach, Laguna Woods, Laguna Hills, Aliso Viejo and Lake Forest. His Republican opponent, Van Der Mark, is a Huntington Beach council member who supported restrictions on certain library materials and the display of Pride flags on city property. Kluwe, 44, spent eight seasons with the Minnesota Vikings from 2005 to 2012, setting eight franchise punting records. Since his playing career ended, he has become increasingly known for his LGBTQ+ activism and outspoken left-wing political views. In a Deadspin article titled "I Was an NFL Player Until I Was Fired By Two Cowards and a Bigot," Kluwe claimed Minnesota released him because of his gay rights activism. The Vikings denied the accusation, maintaining that his release was performance-related. The two sides eventually reached a settlement involving donations to LGBTQ organizations. In 2012, the former punter campaigned against a proposed constitutional amendment banning same-sex marriage in Minnesota and penned a profanity-laced open letter attacking a Democratic Maryland lawmaker who had criticized another NFL player's public support for gay marriage. articles.title: Tom Brady's attempt to play it cool around Erin Andrews raises eyebrows as expert analyses his body language
articles.summary: Tom Brady gave NFL fans something unexpected to talk about during FOX Sports' Thanksgiving pregame show, and this time, it had nothing to do with football.
articles.body: Tom Brady gave NFL fans something unexpected to talk about during FOX Sports' Thanksgiving pregame show, and this time, it had nothing to do with football. The seven-time Super Bowl champion went viral after a seemingly casual interaction with Erin Andrews turned into one of the funniest moments of the broadcast.Brady was part of FOX's Thanksgiving coverage ahead of the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys matchup when cameras caught him patting Andrews on the knee while the crew was sitting together. While the gesture appeared casual, what happened immediately afterward made the moment even more entertaining.Tom Brady's quick reaction brings Kevin Burkhardt into the pictureAfter patting Andrews on the knee, Brady seemingly realized that the cameras had caught the interaction. In what looked like an attempt to make things less awkward, the former quarterback quickly reached over and patted his broadcast partner Kevin Burkhardt on the knee as well.And just like that, Burkhardt became part of the viral moment! The quick sequence caught viewers' attention, with many finding Brady's reaction even funnier than the original interaction. What might have otherwise been an ordinary moment between colleagues suddenly became one of the most talked-about clips from the Thanksgiving broadcast.NFL fans turn Tom Brady's knee pat into a viral jokeAs the clip made its way across social media, fans wasted no time coming up with their own explanations for Brady's quick move. Some joked about the former quarterback's legendary ability to read a situation, with one fan describing it as "He’s a smooth, not surprised." Others couldn't stop laughing at the fact that Burkhardt suddenly received the same treatment.The reactions also included fans suggesting that Brady was simply trying to make sure nobody felt left out. Of course, not everyone saw anything particularly unusual about the interaction. Some viewers pointed out that it appeared to be a harmless moment between colleagues and that there was no reason to read too much into it.Still, the timing of Brady's second knee pat was difficult for the internet to ignore.The Thanksgiving broadcast was supposed to be about football, the rivalry between the Eagles and Cowboys, and the holiday matchup. Instead, Brady's brief interaction with Andrews, followed by his unexpected knee pat toward Burkhardt, gave social media an entirely different reason to talk about the pregame show.And apparently, even after winning seven Super Bowls, Brady can still surprise NFL fans with a move nobody saw coming.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Bears TE Colston Loveland week-to-week with knee injury, reportedly expected to land on IR
articles.summary: Loveland was carted off in the first quarter of Thursday's Bears win over the Lions.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland is considered week-to-week with a knee injury, the team announced on Friday.

Loveland is reportedly going for a second opinion on the injury, which was suffered during Thursday's 39-35 Thanksgiving Day win over the Detroit Lions. He is expected to miss time with what is reportedly a knee sprain, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

A stint on injured reserve is expected, reports ESPN's Adam Schefter , which would rule him out for at least four weeks. The Bears are hopeful that Loveland will return before the end of the regular season and be ready for the playoffs.

Loveland was carted off the field in the first quarter after Lions linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez rolled up on the 22-year-old's left leg as he was engaged in a block for Bears running back D'Andre Swift.

As the second quarter got underway, Loveland was ruled out by the Bears.

Bears head coach Ben Johnson was unsure of the severity of Loveland's injury after the game.

"Nope, don't know yet, no," Johnson said. "We'll find out."

Prior to the injury, Loveland had lost a fumble on Chicago's opening drive, after the ball was punched out by Lions defensive end Derrick Moore. Detroit went three-and-out on the ensuing drive.

Rookie tight end Sam Roush and veteran Stephen Carlson stepped up to fill in the gap left by Loveland: Carlson had two huge catches in the Bears' touchdown drive in the second quarter. The Bears went on to rally for a thrilling win via a go-ahead touchdown in the final seconds.

articles.title: Aaron Glenn needs Jets to win vs. Dolphins to avoid some brutal NFL history
articles.summary: This would be some brutal NFL history if Aaron Glenn and the Jets lose to Miami.
articles.body:
The New York Jets are entering their Week 12 matchup against the Miami Dolphins , one week before their bye, looking for their second straight win this season.

If they beat the 1-9 Dolphins, the Jets will move to 4-8, and their minuscule playoff hopes will remain alive. But a loss would be a crushing blow to any hope of making the playoffs. It would also be a brutal one for Aaron Glenn.

ESPN's Rich Cimini revealed that if Glenn and the Jets lose to the Dolphins in Week 12, then the head coach of the Jets will have made some brutal NFL history as only the second coach in the last 56 years to lose their first 10 divisional games.

Aaron Glenn needs a win to avoid a brutal divisional losing streak

"Embattled coach Aaron Glenn needs a win to avoid becoming only the second coach since the 1970 merger to lose his first 10 division games," Cimini writes.

There is only one other coach in NFL history, since the 1970 merger, to have lost his team's first 10 divisional games. That was Jim Schwartz with the Detroit Lions .

Currently, Glenn is 0-9 against AFC East opponents. With how good the Buffalo Bills and New England Patriots have been the past two seasons, that's not a surprise.

The real surprise here is the Miami Dolphins. Last season, Miami struggled, firing their general manager mid-season, selling at the trade deadline, and finishing with a high pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.

This year, the Dolphins look poised for an even higher pick, likely inside the top five. At 1-9, the Dolphins are easily one of the worst teams in the NFL.

But their lone win this year came against the Jets. If the Dolphins beat the Jets again, this time down in Miami, during the 2026 NFL season, Glenn would likely be en route to a brutal 0-12 record in the AFC East through the first two seasons of his career.

A 0-10 start would already make NFL history. A loss to the Dolphins on Sunday would do just that. While this Jets team has shown some fight this year, there are plenty of issues worth worrying about.

Fortunately for Glenn, the Dolphins are down to backup quarterback Kyle McCord, which should give the Jets an advantage in this one.

A win is far from a guarantee for the Jets on Sunday, but there's reason to be optimistic. If the Jets lose on Sunday, Glenn will have joined Schwarts in some unfortunate NFL history. A win, and Glenn is spared from some more brutal history.

articles.title: Skip Bayless unleashes 5-minute rant on Cowboys’ Thanksgiving collapse that must spell end of Brian Schottenheimer era
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys suffered a Thanksgiving Day stunner, losing on a 60-yard field goal. And it left plenty of blame to go around. Also, the loss sent Skip...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys suffered a Thanksgiving Day stunner, losing on a 60-yard field goal. And it left plenty of blame to go around . Also, the loss sent Skip Bayless on a five-minute rant that must spell the end of the Brian Schottenheimer era, according to his posts on X.

And there's this warning on another post.

"I'm about to unleash a video on the bitter end of this Cowboy season. Schotty must go."

Cowboys have brought Skip Bayless to another rant

Bayless said he felt pretty good when the Cowboys built a 31-10 lead late in the third quarter.

"I'm having a great day, and I'm thinking, finally, for once, I'm gonna enjoy a blowout," Bayless said. "And then that happened."

Bayless spoke about the fourth-down decision by Schottenheimer. The Cowboys went for it on fourth and one with about a minute left. They called a pass play, and Dak Prescott got sacked.

"They go for it, and the play is just a disaster," Bayless said. "The greatest offense there is can't get a yard when it really matters. And that's the essence of this Cowboy team. We can do so much better than (Schottenheimer), can't we? There's no urgency. There's no leadership."

Then Bayless sank further into his annoying pity party.

"I'm actually happy it's over because I'm tired of this," Bayless said. "Just tired of riding the rollercoaster. It's rotten to the core. I'm ashamed of this. I'm sick and tired of this."

The Cowboys fell to 5-7 with the disastrous loss. It pushed them into third place in the NFC behind the front-running Giants (6-3-1) and Commanders (4-5-1). Also, the Eagles (4-7) are within shouting distance of pushing the Cowboys into last place.

Perhaps the worst thing about this is that the Cowboys are basically wasting one of the best seasons of Prescott's career. He's leading the NFL in completions and yardage. How many more years of elite-level play does Prescott have left? And they are also wasting one of the best receiving-duo seasons in NFL history with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.

articles.title: Patriots rule three starters out, major update on Romeo Doubs
articles.summary: The Patriots will be without three starters on Sunday for their matchup against the Chargers.
articles.body:
New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel announced after the team's practice on Friday that quarterback Drake Maye, wide receiver A.J. Brown and cornerback Carlton Davis III will all be unavailable for the team's Week 12 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, according to ESPN's Mike Reiss .

Also, the team is not expecting to get veteran wide receiver Romeo Doubs back from injury for the road game.

Maye suffered a fractured fibula during New England's Week 10 matchup against the Detroit Lions after taking a sack from Lions star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson. He is expected to miss at least six weeks, potentially jeopardizing his availability for the remainder of the regular season. Before going down, Maye completed 65.6 percent of his passes for 2,330 yards, 18 touchdowns and 11 interceptions, while adding 230 yards and three touchdowns on the ground.

Brown is dealing with a hamstring injury that he suffered in Week 10 against the Lions. The superstar receiver has had an injury-plagued season in 2026, having played in only four games to date. He has recorded 11 receptions for 128 yards.

Davis is dealing with a knee injury that has kept him sidelined since November 8. The veteran cornerback has appeared in five games this season, recording two passes defensed and a tackle for loss. His continued absence leaves the Patriots without an important contributor in their secondary.

Doubs is on the verge of returning to action from a shoulder injury that he sustained in Week 6, but given his progress and the capacity in which he practiced with the team this week, is not anticipated to play in Week 12. He has registered 14 receptions for 261 yards and three touchdowns this season.

Follow Patriots Wire on Twitter and Facebook .

articles.title: Seattle Seahawks fans are convinced they know who’ll become the next Dallas Cowboys HC
articles.summary: Brian Schottenheimer appears to have survived yet another tragic loss for the Dallas Cowboys following their Thanksgiving capitulation against the Philadelph...
articles.body:
Brian Schottenheimer appears to have survived yet another tragic loss for the Dallas Cowboys following their Thanksgiving capitulation against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Despite losing another crucial game in the race for the NFC East, Jerry Jones has expressed his trust in Schottenheimer. Defeats like Thursday's will do Schottenheimer no favours in remaining the head coach at AT&T Stadium.

Having already hired the former Seattle Seahawks offensive coordinator, fans up in the Pacific Northwest are convinced that another one of their coaches could be in line to become the next head coach of the Cowboys.

Seattle Seahawks fans think Aden Durde could replace Brian Schottenheimer at the Cowboys

Super Bowl-winning defensive coordinator Aden Durde was previously part of the Cowboys' coaching staff just a matter of years ago. Having shown his quality with the Seahawks, Durde is being projected as the potential replacement for Schottenheimer in Texas.

'Are they smart enough to hire Aden Durde? Real hard to say yes,' one Seahawks fan said on X.

In response to the question about who could replace Schottenheimer, another Seahawks fan simply said: 'Aden Durde.'

Following a stint with the Cowboys as an intern, Durde was later named the defensive line coach in Dallas before moving on to join Mike Macdonald in Seattle. With the Cowboys struggling on defense, a strong defensive mind like Durde could be exactly what Jones needs.

'Aden Durde is a name to watch out of Seattle. He was with the Cowboys already and came over when Macdonald took the head job,' another fan added.

'I predict the Cowboys will fire Schottenheimer and hire Aden Durde,' said another.

This will not be welcome news for Seattle fans, but it is just the reality of your team playing football at the standard they have over the last two seasons. Despite their struggles on offense, Durde's defense has remained rock solid.

'Would Aden Durde be an option? Fits the bargain, familiarity to the Jones boys?' asked another fan.

If Durde does become a head coach, he would become the first ever British head coach in NFL history.

articles.title: Cam Newton now suggests Aaron Rodgers was the reason another player left the Steelers
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers has proven himself to be one of the most controversial characters in NFL history after what has been a blockbuster of a week in the league. The...
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers has proven himself to be one of the most controversial characters in NFL history after what has been a blockbuster of a week in the league.

The Pittsburgh Steelers have released Rodgers from the organisation following his public outburst about head coach Mike McCarthy, with team owner Art Rooney II publicly standing by his veteran coach amid the media frenzy.

Rodgers joined the Steelers last summer, and despite leading them to a winning record last year and thus far in the 2026 season, former quarterback Cam Newton thinks that Rodgers may be the reason that George Pickens left Pittsburgh.

Cam Newton suggests George Pickens left the Steelers because of Aaron Rodgers

Pickens left Pittsburgh to join the Dallas Cowboys in May 2025, with Rodgers joining that summer. However, before Rodgers committed to the Steelers, he trained with DK Metcalf out in California at UCLA's campus whilst a free agent. This is something that Newton feels may have seen the Steelers lose Pickens.

"Who's to say Aaron Rodgers isn't the reason why George Pickens isn't there? Because Aaron Rodgers, while George Pickens was still a member of the roster, went to California. DK Metcalf, who had just previously been signed, was in California when they could have easily brought George Pickens there before George went to Dallas," Newton said on his YouTube channel.

"There are so many different things that Aaron Rodgers was doing that were bad teamship, in my opinion. So now, yes, what he's saying about McCarthy is true. But it's almost the pot calling the kettle black. It's like, bro, you haven't been the stand-up citizen that you're expecting from everybody else."

Only Pickens will know whether Rodgers' decision to train with Metcalf had any impact on his decision to want an exit from Pittsburgh. Losing a receiver as talented as Pickens has certainly proven a blow for the Steelers, given just how badly Metcalf has underperformed.

Having Pickens available for Rodgers could well have made his stint in Pittsburgh more enjoyable and productive. However, it has not panned out in the fairy-tale fashion that the veteran may have hoped for, with his NFL career potentially set to come to an end on the back of this controversy.

articles.title: Commanders CB Amik Robertson to miss second straight game
articles.summary: The Commanders got a win over the Bengals without cornerback Amik Robertson and they'll try to do it again when they face the Cardinals on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Commanders got a win over the Bengals without cornerback Amik Robertson and they'll try to do it again when they face the Cardinals on Sunday.

Robertson remained out of practice this week with an ankle injury and head coach Dan Quinn told reporters on Friday that he will not travel with the team to Arizona. Quinn said the team does not have any long-term concerns about Robertson's injury at this point.

Robertson has 53 tackles, a forced fumble and 10 passes defensed in nine games this season.

The Commanders will release a full injury report later in the day, but Robertson is the only player who has missed practice this week.

articles.title: No, the Rams didn’t run at Micah Parsons
articles.summary: You can’t blame the Packers’ run defense woes against the Rams on Micah Parsons
articles.body:
For the most part, the Green Bay Packers' defense has been solid this season, which is one reason why it was surprising that the Los Angeles Rams were able to run the ball at will against Green Bay on Thanksgiving Eve. This also happened to be the first game that edge defender Micah Parsons returned to the lineup for in 2026, so some people (incorrectly) are lining up dots and saying that the Rams ran at Parsons throughout the game.

I'm here to tell you that this narrative is simply not true.

The video above includes all of Parsons' snaps against the run on Wednesday (13 of them). Maybe twice he was run at in the entire game.

Was the Packers' run defense poor? Yes. Was it because of Parsons? No.

The bigger issue against the Rams was that the interior defensive line was getting pushed back consistently (even against a backup center and backup left guard), and the off-ball linebackers (both backups inserted into the lineup due to injury) had bad nights, too.

articles.title: Why Falcons' Michael Penix Jr. might be in big trouble vs. Vikings in Week 12
articles.summary: This weekend could be a nightmare for Michael Penix Jr.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons are currently 3-7 and are facing off against the 7-3 Minnesota Vikings in Week 12 of the NFL season. For Michael Penix Jr. and this Falcons offense, the Vikings' defense will prove to be a very tricky matchup.

Penix and the Falcons' offense have struggled recently, but the Vikings had a down week against the San Francisco 49ers one week ago. Shouldn't the Falcons have a bit of confidence against Minnesota's highly-touted defense?

In reality, as ESPN's Marc Raimondi highlighted, the Falcons and Penix might be in big trouble this weekend. The Vikings are a horrible matchup for the Falcons' offense, as their high-pressure defense will make life tricky for Penix on Sunday.

Michael Penix Jr. might be in big trouble vs. Vikings

"The Vikings have a league-best 46.2% QB pressure rate, which represents a bad matchup for the Falcons," Raimondi writes. "QB Michael Penix Jr. has the fourth-worst EPA per dropback (minus-0.66) when under pressure this season and the worst completion percentage (34.9%) in those situations."

There aren't many quarterbacks in the NFL who handle pressure as badly, or worse, than Penix has so far this season. Penix is bad under pressure, and that might happen often on Sunday.

This Vikings' defense is elite at generating pressure, with their 46.2% pressure rate being the best in the NFL. Penix and the Falcons' offense haven't faced anything quite like this in 2026.

For a quarterback who struggled under pressure, facing a defense that generates a lot of pressure is sure to be a nightmare matchup.

Unless the Falcons' offensive line can hold up, or Bijan Robinson can make a big difference in the rushing game to avoid needing Penix to throw a lot, the Vikings' defense might torment Penix all day long.

While the Vikings were dominated by the 49ers last week, this defense has been too good to continue to struggle going forward. It would be a surprise if they struggled again in Week 12.

Combined with how bad Penix is when pressured, the Falcons might be in big trouble against the Vikings and Brian Flores' defense this upcoming weekend.

Coming out of the bye, the Falcons are getting about as tough of a defensive matchup as they could draw. The Vikings are a big test for the Falcons, especially with the Vikings' offense improving a lot since their Kirk Cousins acquisition.

articles.title: NFL news, live updates: Jaguars WR Parker Washington out for Week 12 after suffering shoulder injury in practice; Colston Loveland to land on IR with knee injury
articles.summary: Follow along with the latest NFL news in Week 12.
articles.body: Week 12 of the NFL season kicked off with a rare Wednesday matchup between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams, prepping us for a full Thanksgiving feast that delivered fans a full helping of excitement (and then some). Bears-Lions, Eagles-Cowboys and Chiefs-Bills all came down to the wire, allowing no time for a post-Thanksgiving nap.The Denver Broncos and Pittsburgh Steelers will face off Friday in a matchup that will have plenty of eyes drawn — even if not for reasons that are entirely due to the actual football being played on the field. Ahead of that matchup, the Steelers made headlines by reportedly benching veteran quarterback and former MVP Aaron Rodgers in favor of backup Mason Rudolph for Week 12 after recent struggles on offense. This storyline then reached a fever pitch on Wednesday when Rodgers appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" and went scorched-earth on a rant about head coach Mike McCarthy. Rodgers accused McCarthy of repeatedly falling asleep in meetings and ending a team breakdown with "1-2-3 Let's go Packers." Rodgers was released and officially cleared waivers, now free to sign with any team as a free agent.We're watching plenty of injuries ahead of the action, including Las Vegas Raiders All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers, who missed Week 11 with an ankle injury, though he was reportedly pushing to play in that matchup. The Jacksonville Jaguars ruled out WR Parker Washington after he suffered a shoulder injury in practice this week, too, which will have fantasy managers looking for other options on the waiver wire.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more for Week 12.
